ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit, with the output terminal labeled U_o. On the left side, U_i1 is connected through resistor R1 to the inverting input terminal (−) node; the output terminal is connected back through the feedback resistor R_F to the same inverting input node. On the left side, U_i2 is connected through resistor R2 to the non-inverting input terminal (+) node; this non-inverting input node is also connected to ground through resistor R3. Therefore R2 and R3 form a voltage divider for U_i2, setting the non-inverting terminal voltage. Reasoning: From the connection relationship in the figure, the non-inverting terminal voltage V+ = U_i2 * R3/(R2 + R3). Given R2 = R3, so V+ = 5 V * 1/2 = 2.5 V. An ideal op-amp under linear negative feedback has V− = V+ = 2.5 V. Write KCL for the inverting input node: (V− − U_i1)/R1 + (V− − U_o)/R_F = 0. Also because R1 = R_F, obtain (V− − U_i1) + (V− − U_o) = 0, namely U_o = 2V− − U_i1 = 2*2.5 V − 10 V = -5 V.
